description: Table 3 is a table rendered as an image (chart_table); there are no axes, curves, micrographs or scale bars. The header row contains six columns: "Specimen", "Solution temperature (°C)", "YS (MPa)", "UTS (MPa)", "TE (%)" and "f_γ (%)". Four data rows list one solution-treated specimen each: H70 (700 °C) with YS 642.1 MPa, UTS 778.3 MPa, TE 23.0% and f_γ 12.2%; H80 (800 °C) with YS 587.8 MPa, UTS 724.5 MPa, TE 30.5% and f_γ 20.7%; H90 (900 °C) with YS 473.6 MPa, UTS 846.4 MPa, TE 32.0% and f_γ 33.8%; H100 (1000 °C) with YS 398.3 MPa, UTS 860.3 MPa, TE 15.0% and f_γ 12.9%. Reading down the columns, YS falls monotonically as the solution temperature rises (642.1 → 398.3 MPa) while UTS rises monotonically (778.3 → 860.3 MPa). TE and the austenite volume fraction f_γ are non-monotonic: both peak at H90 (32.0% and 33.8%) and fall sharply for H100 (15.0% and 12.9%). The table therefore demonstrates that the 900 °C solution treatment gives the best strength–elongation balance, supported by the maximum retained austenite fraction.

observations.observation: Table 3 tabulates four specimens - H70, H80, H90 and H100 - each corresponding to a solution temperature of 700, 800, 900 and 1000 °C respectively.
The table columns are printed as Specimen, Solution temperature (°C), YS (MPa), UTS (MPa), TE (%) and f_γ (%).
YS decreases monotonically with increasing solution temperature: 642.1 MPa (H70), 587.8 MPa (H80), 473.6 MPa (H90) and 398.3 MPa (H100).
UTS increases monotonically with solution temperature: 778.3 MPa (H70), 724.5 MPa (H80), 846.4 MPa (H90) and 860.3 MPa (H100); H80 is the local minimum.
TE peaks at 32.0% for H90 and is lowest for H100 at 15.0%; H70 is 23.0% and H80 is 30.5%.
The austenite volume fraction f_γ peaks at 33.8% for H90 and drops to 12.9% for H100; H70 has the lowest value at 12.2%.
The caption states the table gives the tensile properties and volume fraction of austenite of the solution treated specimens.
The citing text states that H70 retained 12.2% austenite, with nearly all original austenite decomposed to martensite and spheroidal M5C2-carbide.
The citing text states that for H90 the austenite volume fraction increased to 33.8%, matching the f_γ value printed in the table.
The citing text states H100 owns the first-rank UTS of 860.3 MPa but the worst TE of 15%, consistent with the table values.
The citing text states the microstructures were obtained by solution treatment at 700-1000 °C for 1 h, although the soak time of 1 h is not printed in the table itself.
The citing text states the austenite volume fractions listed in Table 3 were calculated (calculated austenite volume fractions), whereas the caption presents f_γ as an experimental quantity.
